name: Apache Iceberg
model: Open table format: SQL tables as Parquet (or ORC/Avro) files plus metadata, read and written by many engines (Spark, Trino, Snowflake...)
engine_note: Not a server: Parquet data files in object storage, tracked by manifests and a metadata file; a catalog holds the pointer to the current metadata
consistency: Per-table transactions by optimistic commit: a writer swaps the catalog's metadata pointer with check-and-put; if another writer won, it retries. Readers see a committed snapshot (spec: serializable isolation). Multi-table needs catalog support.
scaling: Storage scales with object storage; compute is whichever engines you point at it (Spark, Trino, Flink, DuckDB, warehouses), scaled separately.

licence_events.event: Databricks agrees to acquire Tabular, founded by Iceberg's original creators; Iceberg stays an Apache project under Apache 2.0

managed: Databricks Unity Catalog managed Iceberg tables
version_note: Java library release. Table spec: format v3 adopted; v4 'under active development and has not been formally adopted'.
reach: Reach for it when several engines (Spark, Trino, DuckDB, a warehouse) must read and write the same big tables in your own object storage.
avoid: Avoid for small data or per-request app writes: each commit writes files and metadata, so many tiny commits are slow and need compaction.
escape: data too large for one database, kept as open files in object storage that any engine can query
chat: Long-term archive of all messages and usage events in S3 as tables, for training data and analytics.
notes: Table format, not a server: engine 'columnar' and deploy ['self_hosted','managed'] per the atlas convention. Spec quotes (fetched 2026-10-04): 'An atomic swap of one table metadata file for another provides the basis for serializable isolation'; the file-system rename commit scheme 'is deprecated ... unsafe in object stores'. Tabular: Databricks blog says announced 2024-06-04, completed 2024-06-07 (creators Ryan Blue, Daniel Weeks, Jason Reid). Managed list: S3 Tables evidenced only via a duckdb.org post link and Databricks managed Iceberg via the Databricks transactions page; Snowflake Iceberg tables and Google BigLake not re-fetched today.
